newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Airlines buying into MacroAsia.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Airlines buying into MacroAsia.

text.p: Philippine Airlines on Tuesday said it was buying 70 percent of inflight catering firm MacroAsia Corp, a move that led to some talk in the stock market that the airline was seeking a "back door listing".
The buy-in caused a stir on the Philippine Stock Exchange with MacroAsia shares rising 20 centavos to close at 5.70 pesos from the previous day's close of 5.50 pesos.
At mid-session, it rose to a high of 5.80 pesos.
"Since it seems that backdoor listing is in vogue, that was the immediate reaction to that," Regina Manzano, an investment analyst at Philippine Asia Equity, said.
"PAL board of directors approved on Monday, March 24, the purchase of 700 million pesos worth of capital stocks of MacroAsia Corp," a Philippine Airlines statement said.
"The PAL board describes the investment as strategic in line with the flag carrier's vision to be Asia's best by year 2000," it added.
The 700 million shares, which were priced at one peso each, will be taken out of MacroAsia's authorised and unissued shares.
Manzano was not convinced that PAL would use MacroAsia as a vehicle to tap the equities market.
"Backdoor listing" refers to firms taking over listed companies and gaining access to the stock market as a result, instead of going through the cumbersome procedures for a new listing.
"Being a public company will subject PAL to public scrutiny -- will Lucio Tan want that to happen?" she said.
Lucio Tan, who built his business empire from manufacturing cigarettes and liquors and has the reputation of being the richest man in the country, is the majority shareholder of PAL.
Tan shuns publicity, keeping most of his businesses as tightly held as possible.

ING Barings Securities chief strategist Alex Pomento dismissed the speculation of a backdoor listing, saying PAL had just formalised its entry into a company with which it had a long standing relationship.
MacroAsia took over inflight catering services from PAL after the airline decided to spin off its catering services.
When asked about the backdoor listing talk, MacroAsia corporate secretary Gemma Santos said: "I'm not about to add to the speculation." She declined to say anything further.
Philippine Airlines chief financial officer Jaime Bautista was not available for comment.
The airline is on an expansion programme, recently doubling its capital to 20 billion pesos to support its aggressive re-fleeting programme.
PAL has been borrowing from the international capital market but was unable to tap the local equities market since it needed a track record of profitability before being allowed to list.
PAL officials have said the airline is expected to post losses of about two billion pesos in the current fiscal year ending March. It lost 2.18 billion pesos in 1995/96.
After three straight years of losses, the airline has said it hopes to return to profitability in 1998 as the stepped-up delivery of new aircraft improves operations.
Aside from catering services, MacroAsia has interests in the helicopter rental business and real estate development.
MacroAsia used to be the dormant Cobertson Holdings Corp before it was taken over by a group led by president Jose Tanjuatco and chairman Wee Ah Kee.
